fieldContract.receiptId: Stable identifier for one attempted route execution. Format R-###.
fieldContract.route: Route identifier from search-strategy section 1, or the retrieval-stratum family.
fieldContract.label: Human-readable name of the attempt.
fieldContract.platformEndpoint: The exact endpoint or interface used.
fieldContract.platformVersion: Platform version or the platform-specific version evidence, where the platform reports one.
fieldContract.transport: GET, POST, or manual, as actually used.
fieldContract.transportRule: Measured full GET URL length and the threshold that selected the transport, for PubMed strings.
fieldContract.getObserved: HTTP status returned to the GET attempt, where both transports were attempted.
fieldContract.postObserved: HTTP status returned to the POST attempt, where both transports were attempted.
fieldContract.submittedQuery: The query string exactly as submitted, before URL encoding.
fieldContract.httpStatus: HTTP status of the recorded response.
fieldContract.resultCount: The platform's own count for the submitted query.
fieldContract.recordsRetrievedIntoScreening: How many records this attempt actually pulled into the screening flow, counting both records new to the flow and already-screened records the attempt returned again. 0 marks a route-level count that was recorded but not used for retrieval, or a route that returned nothing resolving to a screening record. The sum of this field over every receipt equals screening.reconciliation.recordsRetrieved, because that total is the sum of per-record retrieval events and every retrieval event belongs to exactly one receipt.
fieldContract.returnedQueryTranslation: The querytranslation string PubMed returned, or the query Europe PMC echoed. Mandatory for every PubMed search.
fieldContract.provenance: Why the attempt exists and how it relates to other rows.
fieldContract.purpose: What a retrieval stratum was defined to capture.
fieldContract.routeLevelCandidateCount: The raw size of the candidate pool a route produced before any relevance filter or inspection. It is NOT a screened set and is deliberately held in a separate field from recordsRetrievedIntoScreening, because conflating the two is what made the receipt totals disagree with the screening flow.
fieldContract.screeningCredit: Prose derivation of recordsRetrievedIntoScreening for this receipt, stating how the figure decomposes and, where a record was returned by more than one route, which rule assigned it.

retrievalDesign.statement: Route-level composite counts and the records that entered screening are two different things, and this artifact keeps them apart. The six PubMed composites of search-strategy section 5 were executed and their counts recorded, but the records behind them were not all downloaded: S1 through S4 alone return 11,765 records unfiltered, which one session cannot screen record by record with a recorded reason each.
retrievalDesign.rule: R-RULE-1, as amended by the R1 remediation. The record set that enters screening is defined by the six original PubMed retrieval strata plus the two strata added by this remediation (N-RS4a and N-RS7), the complete yield of the Europe PMC fly-family route, the ClinicalTrials.gov Essie route, ten quoted-phrase OpenAlex probes, the two preprint routes, the eight non-English probes on OpenAlex and Europe PMC, backward and forward citation chasing over the included set, the DOAJ article API, and four targeted retrievals. Every stratum is a reproducible Boolean or a reproducible API call whose exact string, count and retrieved total are recorded here, and every record it returned was retrieved and given a terminal state.
retrievalDesign.preSpecification: The strata were defined and their counts measured before any record title or abstract was opened. The ordering is visible in this artifact: the stratum receipts carry the same execution date as the composite receipts, and the screening-flow artifact carries no decision that precedes them.
retrievalDesign.residual: The difference between a composite count and the records retrieved from it is a real recall gap, not a rounding error. It is quantified per route in coverageGaps and repeated as limitation L-1 in the synthesis. This pass is a prototype of the pipeline, not an exhaustive systematic review, and no claim in this task may be read as resting on an exhaustive search.
retrievalDesign.citationChasing: Backward and forward citation chasing was absent from the first pass and is finding I-4. It is now part of the design. Backward chasing collected the referenced_works of every resolvable included source (1,631 distinct works); forward chasing collected the citing works of every resolvable included source (2,219 distinct works). The union, less the seeds themselves, was 3,559 works, of which OpenAlex returned metadata for 3,479. A pre-specified relevance expression over the title (pectoral, pec major, bench press, chest press, chest fly, cable crossover, pec deck, butterfly, fly exercise, flyes, flys, push-up, crucifixo, aperturas, cruce de poleas) retained 841; 96 were already in the flow and 745 were new and were screened to a terminal state. The 2,638 chased works that the relevance expression dropped are a recorded residual, not a screened zero.

cochrane.statement: C1 was not executed. The narrow, client-specific and dated fact is this: on 2026-09-13, from a scripted client sending only the project identifier as its User-Agent, https://www.cochranelibrary.com/ returned HTTP 412 with a cookie-gate page and https://www.cochranelibrary.com/search-manager-help returned HTTP 200. No user-agent substitution was attempted, and the help page was not mined for syntax. The reason C1 was not executed is not that the edge blocked this client: it is that CENTRAL Search Manager is an interactive, subscription-gated interface for which this project has no session, and search-strategy section 6.2 already records that no public API exists for it.
cochrane.consequence: Trial coverage in this pass rests on E1, T1 and O1. CENTRAL aggregates hand-searched and registry trial records that MEDLINE indexing can miss, so the recall loss is real and is carried as limitation L-2.
cochrane.supersedes: This replaces the broader sentence flagged as SBLA-008 R2 finding M-10. The block response is still not stable across dates (403 on 2026-09-11, 419 on 2026-09-12, 412 and 200 on 2026-09-13, depending on the URL), and that instability is itself recorded rather than smoothed.

pubmedComposites.statement: S1 returned 1,646 records unfiltered and 1,303 with the humans filter; S2 returned 2,597 and 2,190; S3 returned 3,739 and 2,871; S4 returned 3,783; S5 returned 53; S6 returned 418. The six retrieval strata pulled 911 PubMed records into screening. The strata are deliberately narrower than the composites and the difference is the recall this pass did not exercise.

coverageGaps.languages: No language exclusion was applied, and the R1 remediation added non-English query vocabulary to OpenAlex and Europe PMC (receipts R-046, R-047) together with the DOAJ article API (R-050). That closed the demonstrated half of finding I-6: both records R1 named as absent were retrieved, and one of them, a Portuguese comparison of the bench press with a machine fly, is now an included source. The structural half of the gap remains. Search-strategy assumption SA2 still holds for every route inherited from the first pass, Europe PMC returned a single hit across all eight non-English probes, and a study with no English title or abstract in an index this project cannot reach is still probably never retrieved. Thirty-nine non-English records were retrieved in the first pass and the remediation added more; the translation ladder is recorded per record in the screening flow.
coverageGaps.publisherBlocks: Wiley (onlinelibrary.wiley.com), Elsevier and ScienceDirect, MDPI PDF and the NATA journals platform returned HTTP 403 or an interstitial page to this scripted client. No workaround was attempted. Records behind those blocks whose only eligible contribution needs the full text are recorded as awaiting-full-text.
coverageGaps.citationChasing: Closed as a design gap and disclosed as a bounded one. Chasing now exists (R-048, R-049) but forward chasing is truncated at 200 citing works per seed, two of 76 included sources did not resolve to an OpenAlex work and contributed no references, and the relevance expression that reduced 3,479 chased works to 841 is a recall filter whose residual is quantified above rather than screened.
coverageGaps.registries: Only ClinicalTrials.gov was queried. WHO ICTRP, ISRCTN, ReBEC, ANZCTR, CTRI, ChiCTR, UMIN and IRCT were not. R1 finding M-7 records that the registry conclusion was independently corroborated on ClinicalTrials.gov and ISRCTN by the reviewer, so the conclusion is not in doubt, but the warrant from this project own searching remains thin and is stated as such wherever a registry-based absence is asserted.
coverageGaps.databases: SPORTDiscus and Web of Science were not searched by this project; neither has a public unauthenticated API and this project holds no subscription. Finding I-2 showed this cost a synthesis-level source sitting on the review question. That source has now been retrieved directly (R-051) and is an included source, and its own PRISMA flow covers both databases to March 2023, so the gap is partially mitigated by citation rather than closed by searching.

platformFindings.finding: PubMed proximity distance 0 matches its two terms adjacent in either order, so "machine fly"[tiab:~0] retrieves records containing "on-the-fly machine learning". Thirty-nine records in this pass were retrieved by that artefact alone and are excluded under the new code E-REC-5.
platformFindings.evidence: The 30-term fly-family stratum N-RS1 returned 77 PubMed records, of which 25 are materials-science or computer-science papers whose abstracts contain the phrase "on-the-fly machine learning". This also explains the inflated "machine fly"[tiab:~0] index diagnostic of 32 recorded in the SBLA-008 strategy.
platformFindings.recommendation: Replace "machine fly"[tiab:~0] with an ordered form or drop it and rely on "pec deck", "pectoral deck" and the explicit fly spellings. Route to Codex and to the next evidence round; this role does not own the SBLA-008 strategy file.

platformFindings.finding: The SBLA-008 transport rule holds and extends. Unanchored S2 measured 4,098 characters of full GET URL and returned HTTP 200 on GET; the same string with the humans filter measured 4,129 characters and returned HTTP 414 on GET and HTTP 200 on POST; with the humans and adult filters it measured 4,157 characters, again 414 on GET and 200 on POST.
platformFindings.evidence: Receipts labelled PubMed S2-unfiltered, S2-humans and S2-humans-adult.
platformFindings.recommendation: The 3,700-character operating threshold remains conservative and correct. The observed boundary recorded at scope time (4,121 passing, 4,122 failing) is consistent with these measurements.

platformFindings.finding: OpenAlex title_and_abstract.search is a relevance search unless the term is quoted. Unquoted "cable fly" returned 719 works; quoted "cable fly" returned 4 on the same date.
platformFindings.evidence: Receipts for the O1 probes, both forms recorded.
platformFindings.recommendation: Every OpenAlex probe in this pass uses the quoted form. Any future OpenAlex route should quote its phrases or record that it is running a relevance search.

platformFindings.finding: Europe PMC supports a proximity operator. See unresolvedItems.SU7 for the four discriminating counts.
platformFindings.recommendation: Tighten E1 to proximity form in the next evidence round.
